title: Automation: macros, Office Scripts and Python

questions.question: How do you show the Developer tab in Excel for Mac?

answerOptions.text: File > Options > Customize Ribbon
answerOptions.rationale: That is the Windows path.

answerOptions.text: Tools > Excel Add-ins > tick Developer
answerOptions.rationale: Excel Add-ins is for Solver and the ToolPak, not ribbon tabs.

answerOptions.text: Excel > Preferences > Ribbon & Toolbar, tick Developer, Save
answerOptions.rationale: This is the Mac path; the tab then stays on.

answerOptions.text: View > Macros > Show Developer
answerOptions.rationale: There is no such command.

questions.question: You record a macro in a normal workbook, press Command S, and Excel warns about a macro-free workbook. What should you do?

answerOptions.text: Click Yes to save as .xlsx
answerOptions.rationale: Saving as .xlsx removes the macro.

answerOptions.text: Save as CSV
answerOptions.rationale: CSV keeps only values, so the macro is lost.

answerOptions.text: Ignore it, because macros are saved to OneDrive
answerOptions.rationale: VBA macros live inside the file, not in OneDrive.

answerOptions.text: Click No, then save as Excel Macro-Enabled Workbook (.xlsm)
answerOptions.rationale: Macros are kept only in macro-enabled files.

questions.question: You want a macro that bolds the active cell and the two cells to its right, from wherever you start. What must you switch on before recording?

answerOptions.text: Use Relative References
answerOptions.rationale: Relative recording remembers moves from the starting cell, not fixed addresses.

answerOptions.text: Nothing; the default records relative moves
answerOptions.rationale: The default is absolute, so it always formats the same cells.

answerOptions.text: Store macro in Personal Macro Workbook
answerOptions.rationale: That decides where the macro is stored, not how cells are recorded.

answerOptions.text: Excel > Preferences > Security
answerOptions.rationale: Security controls whether macros run, not how they record.

questions.question: The line hdr = Range("A1").CurrentRegion.Rows(1) stops with run-time error 91. What is the fix?

answerOptions.text: Change Dim hdr As Range to Dim hdr As Long
answerOptions.rationale: A range is not a whole number, so that causes another error.

answerOptions.text: Start the line with Set: Set hdr = Range("A1").CurrentRegion.Rows(1)
answerOptions.rationale: Storing a range in a variable needs the word Set.

answerOptions.text: Put the line inside a With block
answerOptions.rationale: With does not assign an object to a variable.

answerOptions.text: Replace CurrentRegion with UsedRange
answerOptions.rationale: The missing Set causes the error with either property.

questions.question: You type =FYEAR(C2) and get #NAME?. What is the most likely reason?

answerOptions.text: C2 holds a date
answerOptions.rationale: FYEAR expects a date, so a date is correct.

answerOptions.text: The FYEAR function is not yet in a module of this workbook, or it is misspelt
answerOptions.rationale: Excel shows #NAME? when it does not recognise the function.

answerOptions.text: The workbook is saved as .xlsm
answerOptions.rationale: .xlsm is exactly how a workbook with VBA should be saved.

answerOptions.text: Custom functions only work inside macros
answerOptions.rationale: A Function can be used in a cell like any built-in function.

questions.question: A Windows colleague's workbook uses ActiveX command buttons. What happens on your Mac?

answerOptions.text: ActiveX controls do not work on Mac; use Form Control buttons for files that must run on both
answerOptions.rationale: Form controls work on Mac and Windows, ActiveX does not.

answerOptions.text: They work after you enable the Developer tab
answerOptions.rationale: The Developer tab does not add ActiveX support on Mac.

answerOptions.text: They work if the file is saved as .xlsb
answerOptions.rationale: The file format does not make ActiveX run on Mac.

answerOptions.text: They work in Excel for the web instead
answerOptions.rationale: Excel for the web cannot run VBA at all.

questions.question: Which statement about Office Scripts is correct?

answerOptions.text: They are stored inside the .xlsm file like VBA
answerOptions.rationale: Office Scripts are saved in OneDrive, not in the workbook.

answerOptions.text: They can show message boxes and open files on your computer
answerOptions.rationale: Office Scripts cannot do either; VBA can.

answerOptions.text: They work with any personal Microsoft account
answerOptions.rationale: They need a work or school (business or education) account.

answerOptions.text: They are written in TypeScript, stored in OneDrive, and run on the web, Windows and Mac
answerOptions.rationale: They need a work or school Microsoft 365 account.

questions.question: J2 defines df with xl("Sales[#All]", headers=True). In I2 you type =PY(df.shape) and get an error that df is not defined. Why?

answerOptions.text: The Mac is offline
answerOptions.rationale: Being offline stops all Python cells, not just this one.

answerOptions.text: shape only works on Excel values, not DataFrames
answerOptions.rationale: shape is a DataFrame property.

answerOptions.text: Python cells run left to right and top to bottom, so I2 runs before J2
answerOptions.rationale: Use cells below or to the right of the cell that defines df.

answerOptions.text: headers=True must be removed
answerOptions.rationale: headers=True makes the first row the column names; it is not the cause.
